about: The hour checksum rule, as made-up rows and the checksums they must give. The server's tests (Python) and the app's tests (Kotlin) both read this file, so the two cannot drift apart. A blob is written as {"hex": "..."}. The key of a checksum is the strap, a bar, and the hour (ts / 3600, rounding toward zero).

cases.name: whole numbers are summed, and each strap and hour stands alone
cases.create: CREATE TABLE `hrSample` (`deviceId` TEXT NOT NULL, `ts` INTEGER NOT NULL, `bpm` INTEGER NOT NULL, `synced` INTEGER NOT NULL, PRIMARY KEY(`deviceId`, `ts`))

cases.name: a column that may be null adds the count of its values after its sum
cases.create: CREATE TABLE `rrInterval` (`deviceId` TEXT NOT NULL, `ts` INTEGER NOT NULL, `rrMs` INTEGER NOT NULL, `seq` INTEGER NOT NULL, `srcChannel` INTEGER, `tsSuspect` INTEGER, PRIMARY KEY(`deviceId`, `ts`, `rrMs`, `seq`))

cases.name: text and blobs give their summed length, and decimals give nothing
cases.create: CREATE TABLE `mixed` (`deviceId` TEXT NOT NULL, `ts` INTEGER NOT NULL, `kind` TEXT NOT NULL, `payload` BLOB, `x` REAL NOT NULL, `note` TEXT, PRIMARY KEY(`deviceId`, `ts`, `kind`))

cases.name: seconds before 1970 round toward zero, so hour 0 is two hours wide
cases.create: CREATE TABLE `hrSample` (`deviceId` TEXT NOT NULL, `ts` INTEGER NOT NULL, `bpm` INTEGER NOT NULL, `synced` INTEGER NOT NULL, PRIMARY KEY(`deviceId`, `ts`))
